entry.name: FEEL
entry.title: FEEL (Force-Enhanced Egocentric Learning): A Dataset for Physical Action Understanding
entry.summary: Custom gloves with 6 Tekscan FlexiForce A301 sensors each (5 fingertips + palm strip), recorded with Meta Aria Gen 1 egocentric video during unscripted kitchen work (both hands); the release adds right-hand lab recordings from a second camera.
entry.hand: Custom glove: 6 Tekscan FlexiForce A301 + Arduino Nano per hand (both hands in Kitchen, right hand in Lab)

sensor.note: One row per video frame. Kitchen force_{left,right}_aligned.csv: sensor0-5 (filtered, baseline-subtracted, normalized; 0 to ~2.5), force (combined contact signal), force_row_idx (-1 = no glove sample); Kitchen/P13 also has raw_sensor0-5 + raw_force. Lab force_aligned_.csv (right hand): sensor0-4 processed + raw_sensor0-4 (ADC counts, 0-565 in P1) + raw_force + force. Masked drift or malfunction intervals are NaN. Sensor-to-finger order not documented.

scale.text: Paper: ~27 h, ~3M force-synchronized frames of kitchen manipulation. Release: 13 Kitchen + 21 Lab participant recordings (622 GB); readable force CSVs index 1.81M frames (Kitchen 1.07M without P05, Lab 0.73M; Lab P20, P21 have no CSV)

entry.access: Hugging Face edessa/feel, ungated, 622 GB: one uncompressed rgb.tar of JPEG frames per participant (0.5-54 GB) plus per-frame force CSVs (0.4-15 MB).
caveats: The release holds video frames and glove force only. Audio, eye gaze, MPS hand tracking, contact labels and contacted-object masks described in the paper are not in it.
Force columns are processed values without units; the README says the preprocessing targets contact detection and that force magnitudes need a different pipeline.
Kitchen/P05 force CSVs are not text: binary content whose sha256 matches the stored LFS object. Lab/P20 and Lab/P21 have frames but no force CSV.

Lab recordings (848x480 frames from a camera behind the participant, right glove, 5 sensor columns) are not described in the paper; the camera is not named. The first Lab/P1 frame shows laptop typing at a desk.
No task labels or episode segmentation: one continuous recording per participant, 3-64 min at 30 fps.
Masked intervals are NaN; the README says to treat them as missing, not zero. Lab/P1 sensor0 and sensor4 are NaN for the whole file.
No timestamps file; frame rate not stated.
The README points to Kitchen/participant_mapping.tsv; the file is not in the repository.
Lab/P21 holds 4,707 JPEGs that OpenCV cannot decode (README).

other: recorded, not released: Aria audio (7 mics), SLAM cameras, IMUs, eye tracking, MPS hand tracking and 6-DoF trajectory

sources: https://huggingface.co/datasets/edessa/feel (README.md, preprocess.py, .gitattributes, full repo tree via API)

https://huggingface.co/datasets/edessa/feel force CSVs: Kitchen/P06, P09, P12, P13 (both hands), Lab/P1 (+ before_reprocess), P6, P11, P19; head and tail range reads of every CSV; first 2 MB of Kitchen/P12 and Lab/P1 rgb.tar
unconfirmed: Frame rate not stated. 30 fps is derived from the paper (~3M frames / ~27 h = 30.9 fps) and fits the project-page clip times (Lab/P9 has 19,123 frames and a clip ending at 598.5 s, so its rate is at most 32 fps).

Release frame counts are last frame_idx + 1 of each CSV (range reads): Kitchen 1,072,092 over P01-P04, P06-P13; Lab 733,434 over P1-P19. Estimated from rgb.tar bytes per frame: Kitchen/P05 ~88,600, Lab/P20 ~35,800, Lab/P21 ~9,600. Total ~1.94M frames (~18 h at 30 fps), below the paper's ~3M frames / ~27 h; scale.hours and scale.frames are the paper's figures.
sensors_per_hand=6 from the paper (one per fingertip + a palm strip). Lab CSVs carry 5 sensor columns; whether the Lab glove lacks a sensor is not stated.
The arXiv HTML renders the sensor count as '55' and the range as '4545 N' (duplicated digits from math markup); Sec. 3.1 and Fig. 4 give six sensors per glove and 45 N (~10 lbs).
subjects not stated: 13 Kitchen and 21 Lab folders use separate anonymized IDs; overlap between them is not stated. README calls Kitchen/P12 'the Yianni recording' (author Yianni Karabatis).
scenes=2 counts the release's top-level folders (Kitchen, Lab); the number of kitchens is not stated.

Kitchen frames are 1408x1408 fisheye JPEGs (Aria Gen 1 RGB native); the paper says 1440x1440. Lab frames are 848x480; the first Lab/P1 frame shows the participant's head from behind, so the Lab camera is not head-worn. README mentions unuploaded depth/ directories.
Venue from the project page ('ECCV 2026 (oral presentation)'); arXiv v1 lists none.

Column meaning from the paper (Hampel filter, smoothing, rolling-percentile baseline, normalization by the 99.5th percentile, geometric mean of sensors = combined signal) and preprocess.py (raw_sensorN = original readings; force_aligned_.before_reprocess.csv = backup before participant-specific ignore rules).
Kitchen/P05 force CSVs: 2,767,495 and 2,072,576 bytes with ~8 bits/byte entropy, no gzip/zlib/xz header; sha256 of the left file equals its LFS oid fc6edb82..., so the upload itself is unreadable.

download.format: per participant: rgb.tar (uncompressed tar, members rgb/frame_XXXXXXXXXX.jpg in Kitchen, rgb/NNNNNN.jpg in Lab) + force CSV(s) with one row per frame
download.total_size: 622 GB (622,226,531,457 B in the HF tree)
download.per_episode: rgb.tar 0.5-54 GB per participant; a 20 s window at 30 fps is ~280 MB (Kitchen, ~460 KB/frame) or ~66 MB (Lab, ~110 KB/frame); CSVs 0.4-15 MB
download.partial_fetch: HTTP range requests on rgb.tar: frames are stored in order, so a frame window is one contiguous byte range, located by scanning 512-byte tar headers near the offset estimated from bytes per frame. CSVs are fetched whole.

sample.reason: Public and ungated on Hugging Face; no license in the card, repo or project page, so the collection is re-hosted and labelled 'License not stated'.

episodes.subject: Kitchen P12
episodes.why: README recommends P12 as a higher-quality recording. In the window, left sensors 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 exceed 0.1 for 0.9-3.7 s and right sensors 0, 2, 3, 4, 5 for 2.7-11.8 s; right sensor2/3 are NaN for 13% of the window. Window = the authors' project-page clip.

episodes.subject: Kitchen P13
episodes.why: No NaN in the window on either hand; left sensor0 3.9 s, sensor1 2.3 s, sensor3 1.7 s above 0.1, right sensor4 2.9 s. Only Kitchen participant with raw_sensor columns.

episodes.subject: Kitchen P06
episodes.why: All 6 left sensors above 0.1 for 0.3-1.7 s; right sensor1 4.6 s, sensor3 3.4 s, sensor4 4.6 s. Right sensor2 is NaN for the whole window (masked by the authors).

episodes.subject: Lab P11
episodes.why: All 5 sensor columns above 0.1 for 1.5-3.8 s, no NaN.

episodes.subject: Lab P19
episodes.why: All 5 sensor columns above 0.1 for 2.8-6.5 s, no NaN.

episodes.subject: Lab P6
episodes.why: Sensors 0-2 above 0.1 for 5.3-7.7 s; sensors 3-4 stay below 0.1 but are present (no NaN).

sample.fetch_estimate: ~1.05 GB: 3 Kitchen windows x 600 frames x ~460 KB + 3 Lab windows x 600 frames x ~110 KB, by range requests on rgb.tar; the 12 force CSVs of these participants (~75 MB) are already fetched under the survey scratch directory.
sample.rules_applied: No task labels: the release has 2 environments, so episodes span both (3 two-hand Kitchen, 3 right-hand Lab) from 6 different participants. Windows are the authors' 20 s project-page clips, checked for contact in the force CSVs (normalized value > 0.1 for 1 s or more on at least 3 sensors per glove). 6 episodes, 20 s each, within the 10-60 s rule.
deviations: Window seconds assume 30 fps (not stated); frame ranges are what the converter should use.
Kitchen/P06 right sensor2 and Lab/P6 sensors 3-4 show no contact in their windows; the NaN mask is the authors'.
